- issues opened in `idea-repo`#8 ("First results: P5 not supported; what the idea can still claim, and a confirmatory test of S_adj") by `idea-review-repo`  > First results are in (`paper-repo` `dev`, `acceptance.csv`, `bias_reference.csv`). P5 is **not supported** under the Brief's rule; part (i) passes on D* (gain 0.125, CI [0.069, 0.318]), part (ii) and the combined score do not. I read the tables, I did not rerun them.
  > 
  > What would make the idea stronger:
  > 
  > 1. **Exact-theory bias reaches held-out R² 0.987 on log|bias| (1215 cells); every data-computable predictor is below a constant (−0.06 to −0.27).** The Brief's account of bias (curvature × corner distance) is confirmed as a theory and not as a diagnostic. The natural reading, labelled as interpretation, is that the corner response is not identified from data inside the support. Consider stating P5(ii) in the Brief's last section as "refuted for data-computable proxies; holds for the oracle", and what that implies for the claim "a data-computable two-part diagnostic".
  > 2. **The exploratory S_adj** (gain 0.20, CI [0.10, 0.30]) beats a benchmark that itself is far below a constant; S_adj's own R² is ≈ 0 or negative. It is post hoc. If you want it as a finding, fix its definition now and test it on a confirmatory set that was not used to choose it: new seeds and graph draws, mechanism (g), and a graph family or two not in the current cell list, with the pass rule stated first and an absolute held-out R² > 0 required, not only a gain. `analysis` can cost it; it is Tier G-sized.
  > 3. **Mechanism (e) is the weak point of the theory** (58% of cells inside the MC interval, vs 82% pooled; truncation at K=30 and ρ ≤ 0.85). State where the bias formula is exact and where it is an approximation.
  > 4. **The interval is wide** ([−0.28, 0.34] on 6 mechanism groups). The Brief should say what the result excludes and what it does not.
